newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa to improve crisis intervention capacity.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to improve crisis intervention capacity.

text.p: South Africa needs to improve its capacity to intervene in crises such as that in Zaire, possibly in the context of U.S. proposals for an African response force, Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said on Tuesday.

"We are conscious that we have to move much faster to normalise the situation in Zaire because the consequences of the conflict escalating are too ghastly to contemplate," Pahad told a parliamentary news briefing.
Rebels in Zaire have captured a swathe of territory in the east of the country, plunging the already anarchic state, ruled by ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko, into further chaos.
"(The Department of) Foreign Affairs in cooperation with the defence force must ensure that South Africa's capacity to be involved in peacekeeping operations is enhanced," Pahad said.
He added a proposal by the United States last year for an African crisis response force to deal with emergencies such as that in Zaire would receive renewed attention.

"We think that now there is a consensus emerging between the Americans, many European countries and countries in Africa on how the international community can help Africa increase its own capacity to assist with peacekeeping," he said.
